templates.text: Legs drawn up, arms half-extended, settling into the new world.
Fingers curling and uncurling, body slowly adjusting to gravity.
Face scrunched but relaxing between cries, chest rising steadily.
Body curled inward, seeking the shape it knew, then slowly uncurling.
Limbs unfurl in a jerky sequence, the body finding its new axis against the mattress.
Arms splay outward, then draw back in a reflexive hug, the torso arching gently.
A brief startle sends the arms wide, followed by a slower, more controlled recoil toward the midline.
Legs pedal in the air for a moment before settling into a bent, resting posture.
The spine straightens from its curled position, limbs extending into the space of the bassinet.
Hands open and close rhythmically as the shoulders drop from a tense shrug.
Knees pull up toward the belly, then push down, testing the resistance of the swaddle.
The body gives a full-limb stretch, toes pointing and fingers spreading, before relaxing.
Arms lift and cross over the chest in a self-soothing motion, the head turning side to side.
A slight tremor runs through the extremities, subsiding as muscle tone establishes.
Feet push against the blanket, the hips rising slightly before settling back down.
The newborn's posture shifts from flexion to a more open, extended alignment over {seconds} seconds.
Fingers brush the cheek in a rooting reflex, the arm then falling loosely to the side.
Legs perform alternating kicks, the motion gradually slowing as arousal levels out.
The torso twists slightly, one arm extending further than the other in an asymmetric tonic reflex.
Shoulders rotate inward, then outward, as if mapping the boundaries of the new body.
A gentle Moro fragment: arms abduct partially before being drawn back in by flexion.
The body writhes in a slow, worm-like motion, adjusting to the feel of the sheets.
Hands rise to hover near the face, fingers flexing, then descend to rest on the abdomen.
Hips abduct, knees falling outward in a frog-leg position before returning to flexion.
A series of small jerks travel down the limbs, integrating into smoother, purposeful movement.
The head lifts briefly, causing the shoulders to tense, then all sinks back into the surface.
Arms move in a slow, swimming motion, the palms occasionally turning upward.
Feet dorsiflex, toes fanning, then plantarflex as the legs settle.
The body exhibits a crawling reflex, legs pushing while arms make rowing motions.
Muscle tone fluctuates visibly, from floppy to firm, before finding a moderate baseline.
One leg extends fully while the other remains bent, a common asymmetrical resting pose.
The infant's movements transition from large, jerky arcs to smaller, localized adjustments.
After the initial cry, the body goes still for a beat, then erupts into a wave of limb extension.
Elbows and knees unlock in stages, the body surrendering to the pull of gravity.
Arms extend outward in a slow, asymmetrical reach, then fold back toward the body.
The legs, initially flexed, push downward in a gentle, alternating motion against the surface.
A full-body shudder precedes a gradual extension of the spine and limbs into a more open posture.
Hands flutter near the face before arms descend, palms turning upward in a resting position.
The head turns to one side, prompting a fencing posture that slowly dissolves into symmetry.
Toes fan out and curl back in as the ankles rotate, exploring the new proprioceptive space.
Shoulders drop from a high guard, allowing the elbows to bend and settle at the infant's sides.
A brief Moro fragment—arms lifting—is aborted, transitioning into a smooth limb descent.
The body uncurls in segments: first the spine lengthens, then the legs, finally the arms.
Knees rise and fall rhythmically, the hips swiveling slightly with each movement.
Fingers splay wide in a starfish pattern before softly closing into a loose fist.
The torso arches gently off the surface for a moment, then settles with a sigh.
Limbs move in a fluid, writhing motion that gradually slows to intermittent twitches.
One arm stretches overhead while the other remains flexed, creating a transient asymmetrical tone.
Feet press together, soles touching, as the legs adopt a frogged position before extending.
A wave of extension travels from the shoulders down to the feet, then recedes into flexion.
The newborn's body rocks slightly side-to-side, limbs adjusting to counterbalance the motion.
Palms open and press flat against the blanket, bearing a slight weight before relaxing.
Elbows and knees unlock in a staggered sequence, each joint finding its resting angle.
A startle reflex truncates into a deliberate arm extension, fingers brushing the cheek.
The infant's body yields to gravity, limbs sinking into the mattress with a gradual release of tension.
Alternating leg movements, like gentle cycling, slow as the feet find purchase on the sheet.
Shoulders hunch and then roll back, the scapulae flattening against the bassinet surface.
The hands rise, cross at the wrists briefly, then fall apart to rest on the abdomen.
Muscle tone fluctuates visibly, moving from moderate hypertonia to a more placid state.
A subtle tremor in the chin extends to the arms before being suppressed by stabilizing contractions.
The body makes small, adjusting movements, orienting toward the source of warmth and touch.
Limbs draw inward in a clasp, then slowly push outward, testing the limits of their new domain.
Hips abduct, knees bending outward, then adduct back toward the body's midline.
